plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers that attract bees and butterflies. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields for essential oils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean native; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans used it to scent baths.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads made up of hundreds of tiny florets. The heads track the sun when young and face east when mature.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, the United States, and France
plants.funFact: The spiral arrangement of seeds in a sunflower head follows the Fibonacci sequence, which maximizes seed packing efficiency.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular fragrant flowers rising on tall stalks. The leaves have a water-repellent surface.
plants.location: Asia and northern Australia, including India, China, Japan, and Vietnam; grown in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature to about 30-35°C, even when the air is much cooler, thanks to a heat-producing process similar to that of warm-blooded animals.

plants.name: Eucalyptus leucoxylon
plants.description: A medium-sized Australian tree with smooth mottled bark and clusters of nectar-rich flowers that provide an important food source for native birds and bees during the southern winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter and spring (May to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.funFact: Yellow gum flowers vary in color from cream to deep red, and the cultivar 'Rosea' is a popular street tree that feeds lorikeets and honeyeaters in winter.
